travelAdvisory.summary:
Reissued after periodic review without changes.
Exercise normal precautions in Hungary.
Read the country information page for additional information on travel to Hungary.
If you decide to travel to Hungary:

Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive alerts and make it easier to locate you in an emergency.
Follow the Department of State on Facebook and X/Twitter.
Review the Country Security Report for Hungary.
Visit the CDC page for the latest Travel Health Information rel

healthcare.summary: Health & medication guide for Hungary. Emergency numbers (104/107/105/112), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, travel insurance advice, and vaccination recommendations.

connectivity.simOptions: Telekom, Telenor (Yettel), or Vodafone prepaid SIMs at Budapest airport or city shops. EU roaming with any EU SIM.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at most cafes (Budapest's café culture is strong), hotels, and thermal baths. Good 4G coverage citywide.
connectivity.bestOption: EU SIM with roaming. Otherwise Vodafone prepaid at airport. eSIM via Airalo as quick alternative.

cultural.tipping: 10-15% at restaurants (specify when paying — don't leave on table). Round up for taxis. Tip thermal bath attendants HUF 500-1000.
cultural.dressCode: Smart casual in Budapest. Business dress is formal. Bring swimwear for thermal baths (some require swim caps).
cultural.greetings: Handshake with eye contact. 'Szia' (see-ah) for casual hello. Hungarians put surname first (like Japanese). Close friends may cheek-kiss.
taboos: Clinking beer glasses (relates to 1848 Austrian celebration — some Hungarians still observe this)
Confusing Hungary with other Eastern European countries
Not taking off shoes when entering someone's home
cultural.haggling: Not practiced at shops or restaurants. The Great Market Hall has fixed prices despite being touristy. Watch for tourist-trap restaurants in Váci utca.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free (Schengen). UK, EU, Australia, Canada, Japan also visa-free.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: April-June and September-October (mild, fewer crowds). July-August (hot, festivals). December for Christmas markets and thermal baths.
